title: Firearm possession after a listed misdemeanor conviction
summary: Owning, purchasing, receiving, possessing or controlling a firearm within ten years of a specifically listed misdemeanor conviction. The exact offense, subdivision and conviction date must match 29805(a)(1); not every misdemeanor triggers this branch. Exceptions and the separate 29800(a)/29805(b) branches must be considered. The narrow found-or-taken-firearm defense in 29850 requires every statutory condition and is not a general permission to possess a firearm.
penalty: Wobbler: up to 364 days in county jail or 16 months, 2 years or 3 years in state prison under section 18, a fine up to $1,000, or both fine and custody. Adult base penalties are shown. Predicate matching, exemptions, restoration of rights, constitutional defenses, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing require review. This entry does not determine whether a particular person is prohibited.
mentalState: Knowing ownership, acquisition, possession or control; the exact conviction or known-warrant predicate and applicable period must be established.

The narrow found-or-taken-firearm defense in 29850 requires every statutory condition and is not a general permission to possess a firearm.
penalty: Wobbler: up to 364 days in county jail or 16 months, 2 years or 3 years in state prison under section 18, a fine up to $1,000, or both fine and custody. penalty: Wobbler: up to 364 days in county jail or 16 months, 2 years or 3 years in state prison under section 18, a fine up to $1,000, or both fine and custody. Predicate matching, exemptions, restoration of rights, constitutional defenses, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing require review. title: Ammunition possession by a person with a qualifying firearm prohibition
summary: Owning, possessing or controlling ammunition or reloaded ammunition while subject to a qualifying Chapter 2/3 firearm prohibition or WIC 8100/8103 restriction. The underlying prohibition must actually apply; a diagnosis, arrest or generic criminal record is not enough. The ammunition definition and the limited found/taken-ammunition delivery-to-police defense in 30305(c) require review; that defense does not extend to every prohibited category. For this subdivision, 16150(b) includes bullets, magazines, clips and other specified feeding devices or projectiles; it excludes blanks.

title: Ammunition possession contrary to a qualifying gang injunction
summary: A person not already prohibited by 30305(a) owns, possesses or controls ammunition while personally enjoined under Civil Code 3479 as a member of a criminal street gang defined in 186.22. This subdivision uses the loaded-cartridge definition in 16150(a), excluding blanks; do not import the broader 16150(b) definition reserved for 30305(a).
penalty: Misdemeanor under 30305(b)(2) and 19: up to six months in county jail and/or a fine up to $1,000. Adult base penalties are shown. title: Carrying a concealed firearm within a controlled vehicle
summary: Knowingly carrying a concealable firearm hidden within a vehicle under the person's control or direction. A firearm openly carried in a belt holster is not concealed under 25400(b). Applicable license, residence/business, transportation and other statutory exemptions must be checked; no conclusion about open-carry law follows from this entry. The limited grave-danger justification in 25600 depends on its restraining-order and other conditions; it is decided by the trier of fact.
penalty: Ordinary 25400(c)(7): up to 364 days in county jail and/or a fine up to $1,000. Paragraphs (c)(5)-(6) permit misdemeanor or 1170(h) felony punishment, ordinarily 16 months, 2 years or 3 years. Paragraphs (c)(1)-(4) are felony-only, ordinarily the section 18 state-prison term. Loaded status alone does not establish (c)(6): the ammunition/readily-accessible condition and unregistered-owner condition must both apply. Prior-based minimum jail terms in (d)-(e), including the unusual-case exception, require individual review. No single penalty is inferred from the conduct citation alone. Adult base penalties are shown. Predicate matching, exemptions, restoration of rights, constitutional defenses, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing require review. This entry does not determine whether a particular person is prohibited.
mentalState: Knowledge of the concealed firearm and the branch-specific carrying or causing conduct.
